record.paper_title: Evolutionary dynamics of cancer: From epigenetic regulation to cell population dynamics—mathematical model framework, applications, and open problems
record.context_brief: Entropy production and dissipation in heterogeneous cancer dynamics
record.original_question: For the same non-delay model, let Q(t)=∫_Ω Q(t,x)dx be the total cell number, let f(t,x)=Q(t,x)/Q(t) be the fraction of cells with epigenetic state x, and define the multicellular entropy by E(t)=-∫_Ω f(t,x) log f(t,x)dx. Determine how to decompose the entropy derivative dE/dt into an entropy production rate epr and an entropy dissipation rate edr such that dE/dt=epr-edr and both epr and edr are always nonnegative, and characterize under what conditions the developmental dynamics described by the model—especially cancer development—produce increasing entropy.

evidence.quote: The entropy problem asks: how can we decompose the rate of entropy change into the entropy production rate (epr) and entropy dissipation rate (edr) such that dE/dt = epr − edr,

and both epr and edr are always non-negative? Solutions to this problem are essential to answer the question of how the entropy changes during the process of tissue development. In particular, is cancer development a process of increasing entropy [15, 42]?
For the general situation, it is not known how the entropy production rate and dissipation rate should be defined, and under which situation the development process leads to increasing entropy.

artifact.category_tag: entropy production in cell population dynamics
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ^n be a bounded domain representing the space of epigenetic states of cells. Consider a heterogeneous cell population whose density Q(t,x) ≥ 0 (number of cells per unit epigenetic state at time t) evolves according to the integro-differential dynamics

  ∂_t Q(t,x) = β(x) ∫_Ω p(y,x) Q(t,y) dy − (β(x) + d(x)) Q(t,x),   t > 0, x ∈ Ω,

with prescribed nonnegative birth rate β(x), death rate d(x), and inheritance kernel p(y,x) ≥ 0 satisfying ∫_Ω p(y,x) dx = 1 for every y ∈ Ω (so that p(y,·) is the probability density of the epigenetic state of a daughter cell given that of its mother y). Let

  Q(t) = ∫_Ω Q(t,x) dx,    f(t,x) = Q(t,x)/Q(t),    E(t) = − ∫_Ω f(t,x) log f(t,x) dx

denote the total cell number, the population fraction at epigenetic state x, and the multicellular (Shannon) entropy of the population, respectively.

(a) Find an explicit decomposition

  dE/dt = epr(t) − edr(t)

of the time derivative of E(t) into an "entropy production rate" epr(t) and an "entropy dissipation rate" edr(t), expressed in terms of Q, f, β, d, and p, such that epr(t) ≥ 0 and edr(t) ≥ 0 hold for all t > 0 and all admissible initial data.

(b) Characterize the conditions on β, d, and p (and on the initial distribution f(0,·)) under which the developmental dynamics yield monotonically increasing entropy E(t), i.e. dE/dt ≥ 0 for all t > 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open question in the cancer evolutionary dynamics literature: a general definition of nonnegative entropy production and dissipation rates for such heterogeneous cell-population models, and conditions under which the entropy is increasing, is stated to be unknown. No subsequent work establishing such a general decomposition for this model class was located.
